EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the typical “benzaldehyde triad”: a very strong C=O stretch at 1700 cm⁻¹, an aromatic C=C stretch at 1600 cm⁻¹ and the benzene ring-breathing mode at 1004 cm⁻¹ – all characteristic of an aromatic aldehyde. Peaks at 619 cm⁻¹ and 653 cm⁻¹ fall in the aryl C–Cl stretching region (∼600-700 cm⁻¹), indicating a chloro-substituent on the ring. Candidates 1, 3 and 4 lack a C–Cl bond, whereas candidate 2 (O=Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1, a chlorobenzaldehyde) contains a single aldehyde and one C–Cl bond, matching both the carbonyl and the ∼620/650 cm⁻¹ bands without introducing extra functional-group bands that would be expected for the more heavily substituted sulfur-containing structures (5, 6, 7) or the non-aromatic molecules (8–10). Thus candidate 2 best fits the peak pattern.
